note: Switch "commission" (off by default; island games only): when you muster the army you choose who leads it, yourself or a named man. If you go, you name a keeper of the citadel, plots at home get easier while you are away, and the keeper's loyalty enters your defense. A man you send comes home popular if he wins. Every price is shown before you muster. The pattern is in the sources below; every rule and number here is invention.

sources.name: Dionysius led his army in person

facts.quote: while he himself, profiting by a moonless night, made a circuit with his army
speedily collected as many Syracusans and mercenaries as he could and set forth

sources.name: Andron keeps the fortress while the ruler is away

facts.quote: When Dionysius left on a foreign expedition, he left Andron in charge of the fortress and the treasury
Hermocrates advised Andron to seize both of these, while Dionysius was absent

sources.name: Syracusans armed for the war turn on the tyrant

facts.quote: they hoped that once they had got weapons in their hand, they could strike for their liberty
without his presence, had won a victory over the Carthaginians, they were now puffed up with pride
now because of the war they had weapons at their command

sources.name: Syracuse's cavalry sacked the absent Dionysius' house

facts.quote: they rode off with one accord to Syracuse
plundered the house of Dionysius which was filled with silver and gold
